chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions, from al-Washsha, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The deceased is not to be shrouded in black.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: is shrouded (passive verb referring to wrapping the body in cloth for burial)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended or disliked color for shrouding the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against shrouding the deceased in black, a ruling that distinguishes Shia funerary customs from other traditions and reflects the preference for purity and light in death rituals. This narration is recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on recommended and disliked burial attire, highlighting the Ahl al-Bayt's emphasis on symbolic cleanliness and simplicity in the transition to the afterlife.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Al Washha, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not enshroud the deceased in black’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of his people from al-Washsha’ from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A deceased is not shrouded in black.’”
